item: A CHECKPOINT before every shard's aggregate lets the in-memory rollup build reach 28 M mentions at 1,004 MB (R169), and a plain out-of-memory error is named at its stage
summary: The in-memory rollup stays in uncompressed write buffers until something checkpoints it, so the rollup alone was hundreds of MiB by the last shards. columnar._checkpoint now runs before each shard's aggregate (same classification as the final compact: an allocation FatalException is a duckdb-limit stop at stage checkpoint with the shard, any other fatal is the unusable-instance failure, any other error carries on and is counted); plan_build_shards is unchanged. A plain OutOfMemoryException in a staged insert is the same wall: a type-only _PlainEngineWall turns it into a duckdb-limit stop at stage-insert or keywords with engine_error_class OutOfMemoryException (before, a raw error and a stage-less skip); interrupts still propagate raw and no engine text is kept. MEASURED (DuckDB 1.5.6, memory_limit 1,004 MB, no offload, 2 threads, 16 GB machine, poller-free, seeded corpora of 8 mentions per keyword): the base build (a checkpoint only after the build) built 16 M (7 of 7), declined at 20 M (0 of 8, keywords-stage FATAL), raised a raw OutOfMemoryException at 24 M (2 of 2) and declined at the last shard at 28 M (2 of 2); with a checkpoint before every shard it built 20 M (5 of 5), 24 M (2 of 2) and 28 M (2 of 2). WHICH CODE: the keyword-machine 20, 24 and 28 M cells at 1,004 MB ran the bench's patched aggregate (it checkpoints first), not the shipped columnar._checkpoint; the shipped code itself was measured in Export's 28 M runs and in the 600 and 450 MB runs. Boundary reads / resident after the final compact (MiB): 16 M 199 / 81, 20 M 241 / 99, 24 M 280 / 121, 28 M 288 / 135. 28 M also BUILT at 600 MB (2 of 2) but the serve check (canary) passed in 1 of the 2 (the other read out-of-memory, which the app keeps as a duckdb-limit stop at stage serve-check and does not serve), and it was declined at 450 MB (2 of 2, stage keywords, OutOfMemoryException): the BUILD floor at 28 M lies between 450 and 600 MB, not narrowed further, and 600 MB is not shown to be above the SERVING floor. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED by the Export lane on another machine (same generator, 28 M at 1,004 MB): boundary reads 288.1, resident after build 453.8, after compact 134.8 to 135.0 and every parity digest (per-term counts and ranked values, 7 d, 30 d, all) equal to the digit, and the base build declined at the same stage, shard and class (aggregate, shard 34, FatalException). DuckDB-accounted memory (duckdb_memory(), what memory_limit enforces) is the figure; process high-water is PER MACHINE and includes the interpreter: 691 to 695 MiB on the keyword machine (about 83 MiB baseline) against 738 to 779 on Export's (124 to 125 MiB measured baseline). OPEN: whether the real checkpoint adds about 23 MiB of process memory over the bench's patched aggregate (Export: 765 and 779 against 738 and 759, n=2 each, ranges do not overlap but the spread is the same size; not isolated; DuckDB's counters are identical). NO wall-clock claim (machine-dependent: Export's seconds were 40 to 50 percent shorter). Query parity (digests of the per-term counts and of the ranked top-80 values per window, not of the rollup's rows): base and per-shard-checkpoint identical at 16 M (4 runs). KNOWN LIMIT: the all-history top terms return 0 rows (the live scan answers, counted in serve_fallbacks) from 20 M mentions up and at 16 M with a 600 MB limit. NOT CLAIMED: any ceiling above 28 M; any other machine. THE 8 MACHINES OF THE 16 OCTOBER BUNDLES (28.9 to 33.4 M mentions, limit 738 MiB): #1427 attempts the build on them with no up-front decline (plan_build_shards returns fits=False at 35 to 38 shards and nothing reads it; BUILD_CODE_VERSION is bumped to 3 in this PR, so a stop kept by any earlier code is released on upgrade and the build is tried again); whether the build fits 738 MiB at 29 to 33 M is UNMEASURED here.
